title: Arrays
bridge: C arrays are fixed-size rows of one type: `int scores[5] = {72, 85, 90, 64, 70};`. They **don't know their own length**, so functions take the array *and* a count: `double average(const int a[], int n)`. Indexes run 0 to n-1 and nothing checks them.

exercises.title: Average of an array
exercises.prompt: Write double average(const int a[], int n): the average of the n items, or 0 when n is 0.

tests.hint_if_fail: With n == 0 there's nothing to divide by.

hints: Loop i from 0 to n-1 adding a[i].

exercises.title: Biggest reading
exercises.prompt: Write int max_of(const int a[], int n) (n is at least 1): the largest value. It must work when every value is negative.

tests.hint_if_fail: Starting best at 0 beats every negative number. Start at a[0].

hints: What if every value is below 0?
int best = a[0]; then loop from i = 1.

quiz.q: How does a C function know an array's length?
choices: You pass the count as another parameter
quiz.why: Inside the function, the array is just an address.
